text.global.d.ts: Defines renderer IPC bridge contracts, including the pull request refresh and enter-a-pull-request calls, the extensions load, save, move, create-a-skill, skill linker and import-a-list calls, provider, user settings, Codex hook, lantern command, macro view and RTK status types, the add-folder result with its selected path, the memory watch call and its update push, the free-memory call, the ask-for-the-editor-server call, the project name, branch and worktree call, the account status, project, add-token, rename, expiry, commit-email, bind, unbind and remove calls with their change push, the explain-a-file calls and completion push, the notification card with its per-card preferences and overlay bridge with its open and jump-to-terminal calls, the dev-build identity call, the menu bar popover bridge with its model and open pushes, and shared response types
text.lantern-flow.css: Styles the Flow view of a pull request: each story as a numbered card with a track that joins its rows, kind-coloured blocks linked by arrows (stacked in one column when the flow itself is narrow, measured by a container query), a person icon on actors, old and new texts stacked, the file chips under a step with a +, ~ or − mark (plain chips when a question's flow is drawn), the picked step (amber border and glow that win over hover) and the list rows it marks, and the reading ring and badge on steps that mention the open file with the other steps greyed; focus rings and reduced motion included
text.lantern-macroview.css: Styles the Macro view's areas map: the map's shapes, labels, marks in both themes, the one dashed outline (features not in an area yet), the solid wash-and-thin-outline of a place a selected platform only uses, the legend's swatches, the zoom controls, the fixed-height outside systems list under the map with its count pills, the overview drawer with its scrim, and hides the host's own zoom bar while it is shown
text.lantern-plans.css: Styles the Plans strip, the Planning view split (plan on the left, Macro or Files on the right) and the plan panel: state badges for draft, approved and stale, the sticky plan header, full-height plan column, the plan bar and the rules that hide the project list, tabs and strips while a plan fills the window (the app bar is hidden, one shared inset clears the macOS traffic lights for the bar, and the window drags by the bar), the plan and map divider, foldable stage cards with a blocked or done edge and a progress bar, item status pills, questions, grouped impact rows with new and related files, the approval table, pull request links, touched targets and the pick note, and the question buttons, the answers bar and the question modal with its help buttons, notes and help boxes, and the problems note with its scrolling list and the bar to copy the problems or fix them with an agent, and the Copy plan text button in the plan header
text.lantern-prs.css: Styles the pull request tabs in the map's head row (branch name, state pill in open, merged, closed or declined colours, dismiss, restore and add-local-review buttons), the pull request hover card (author avatar or initials, dates, file counts by kind, approvals), the sidebar header card with its story and bottom action bar (details toggle, Refresh, Open PR), the Context box of a local comparison, file lists with missing-reason markers, review controls, the described sections, the pull request summary and the only-this-pull-request toggle, and the compare dialog with its pickers
text.lantern-relation.css: Styles locked relation inspection and related file notices
text.lantern-review.css: Lays out the pull request review as file list, file or diff pane and graph, with the draggable dividers, a grid for every combination of hidden areas, the restore buttons on the edges, the Explain more row under the reason with its sections and collapsed header, and the inline review comments: the gutter plus, floating Comment button, comment box with text chips and the Fix, Explain or Question choice, cards under their lines with a quiet intent label and file comments, header tools with the Copy all default intent and the comment list popover
text.lantern-sections.css: Styles the section buttons in the map's toolbar row and the project section overlays: access matrices, state diagrams, schema filters, tables and fact lists
text.lantern-select.css: Lets the readable text of the review screens be selected and copied (the pull request header, its described sections, list reasons and file names, the reason row and its explanation, code and diff lines, Flow texts and chip names, the side panel sentences, and the whole plan panel including its item, stage and question buttons but not its copy and close buttons) while the chrome, the page and the graph canvas stay unselectable
text.lantern-setup.css: Styles map setup progress and agent logs
text.lantern.css: Styles the map panel: its head row, the single toolbar row with platform tabs, the Files and Macro view switch and the Macro level breadcrumb with its hidden level announcer, graph navigation, file and block details with their plain-sentence relations and the by-area list of what talks to an outside system, the Macro legend key and its two help lines, code preview dialogs, rendered Markdown and the diff colours the review pane shares, with the base and branch picker shown when a diff has no base, and the bottom status bar: the session state dot, map stats with their icons, the problems button with its error, warning and notice counts and the list that opens above it, the toast placement and fade-in, integration icons with a missing mark, and the assistant picker menu; its map colour tokens also apply to the pull request hover card
text.memory.css: Styles the memory view: summary strip, category bars, project and process tables with the old-and-large highlight, narrowing by container width
text.overlay.css: Styles the notification card: a tint in the colour of its kind over the native blur, header chip, queue badge, countdown close button and open button
text.overlay.html: Bootstraps the desktop notification card surface with the shared theme, its own styles and the tooltip and popover styles
text.tray-popover.css: Styles the menu bar popover: the app's navy tint over the native blur, the logo tile, the count pill in the colour of the most urgent state, grouped project rows with a drawn state indicator, the footer buttons, the More panel and the empty state, with a spinner that stops when motion is reduced
text.tray-popover.html: Bootstraps the menu bar popover surface with the shared theme and its own styles
text.tray-popover.ts: Mounts the popover view on the page and feeds it the model the window opens with and every change pushed while it is open
text.overlay.ts: Turns on the shared tooltips, connects the notification window to its card stack and plays each arriving card's sound with the volume and timbre chosen for its kind
text.settings.css: Styles the settings editor: search header, category list with a panel group, setting rows, the command line and RTK panels, problem notices and the dialog footer, plus the slider, choice, sound preview and screen-position picker controls
text.state.ts: Shares active project, editor tabs with the time each was last selected, the editor server's grace time, whether the Editor was asked for, and per-project map preferences, dismissed pull requests included
text.theme.css: Defines the Lantern brand fonts, colours (including the secondary button and strong border tones), notification kind colours, type scale and control sizes shared by the workspace and the notification window
text.workspace.css: Imports the shared theme and defines the Skills modal tabs, the Lantern skills board (the role selector, the attached and attachable columns, scope badges, search box and built-in group, stacking at narrow widths) and the Skill linker view and the linker state line and the refresh button whose glyph spins in place, with its missing-skill warning and the add-skill step's stacked fields and text area, the full-width app bar (project identity, the centred Search commands field and the Editor/Lantern switch, fixed over the sidebar and the map, macOS drag area and traffic-light inset, hidden in a pop-out), the offset of the sidebar and main area for it and for the map's status bar, the project filter and list rows with their active and keyboard focus marks and the Free memory and Remove from sidebar buttons, the status note, which is hidden once the editor is ready along with its footer, the project-window layout, provider and Codex hook set-up and remove controls, loading covers and tool modal presentation, and a coloured dev-build banner strip along the bottom of the app bar that makes the bar taller.
text.workspace.html: Bootstraps the workspace shell: the app bar with the project name, branch and linked worktree, the Search commands field with its shortcut and the Editor/Lantern switch, then the sidebar with the project filter and its match count, the hidden Lantern tools assistant picker, Codex hook set-up and remove buttons, the Enable mic button, the stylesheet of the Plans strip and plan panel, the settings editor, command palette and Integrations styles, and the Skills, Memory and Explain dialogs, holds the hidden dev-build banner under the app bar, gives its buttons their hover text in data-tip with an accessible name of their own, and lets editor frames load from any loopback port
text.workspace.ts: Turns on the shared tooltips with the key chips of a command's current binding, registers the commands that shortcuts, the application menu and the command palette run, including explain.open, integrations.open and lantern.problems and lantern.refresh (they bring the map to front first), mounts the command palette and the app bar's project identity, closes the palette before a command pushed from main runs, runs the ones main pushes, initializes project navigation with a filterable project list whose active row is marked and revealed, embedded editor tabs, tools, user settings state and the per-project assistant choice, opens or activates the folder picked in the add-folder dialog, and claims its own project in a project window, marks the body as macOS so the app bar clears the traffic lights in every window, showing a finished session with a background task still running as needing attention, dropping a startup settings snapshot that a later push superseded, closes project tabs that stay idle when the setting is on and the server frees idle hosts, and wires each project row's Free memory and Remove from sidebar buttons and the status note they leave and hiding the status line until the Editor is asked for and once the editor is ready, and the server loading screen, which covers an Editor tab or a waiting Editor request in front and never the map, and the Editor/Lantern switch that opens the map or shows the editor and asks main to start the server the first time (bringing the map to the front by any route cancels the wait; a project opens in the map straight away, without an editor tab, until the server is up or when there is no VS Code CLI), and, in a dev build, asks main which worktree build this is and shows its banner in the build's colour with the name, branch and folder, and puts the name in the window title.
text.integrations.css: Styles the Integrations screen: provider sections and logos, the jump-to-projects button, account rows with expiry warnings and the commit email line, the add-account form with its help, the project tiles and a project's detail, narrowing by container width
text.command-palette.css: Styles the command palette: the borderless card that slides open from the app bar's search field (under the bar when the field is hidden), the search field, the rows with their highlighted matches, group labels and shortcut chips, and the selected row
text.svg.d.ts: Types imported .svg files as their markup string
text.floating.css: Styles the shared floating layers drawn in the top layer: the tooltip (a small dark box with its shortcut chips, or a wider card for rich content such as the pull request hover card) and any popover anchored to its trigger with four placements and flip fallbacks, both fading and sliding in and out unless reduced motion is asked for
